correctness.rationale: For pairwise distinct primes 3,r,q, multiplicativity and the exact prime-power divisor definitions yield 28(r²+1)(q+1)=30(r²+r)q; solving gives q=14-210(r-1)/(r²+15r-14), so 0<q<14. Excluding q=3 and requiring primality restricts q to 2,5,7,11,13. The quadratic in r has discriminant Δ(q)=281q²-728q-784. Direct exact recomputation found Δ=-1116,2601,7889,25209,37241 respectively; only 2601=51² is a nonnegative square, and q=5 factorization 9r²-75r+84=3(3r-4)(r-7) forces prime r=7. At r=7,q=5, both divisor sums equal 8400 for 3³7²5=6615. This is a complete infinite-prime-pair proof by a bounded q inequality and integer discriminants; numerical prime searches are not used as proof.
